description: CAD bake-off 1 of 3 -- OPENSCAD: build the SO-101 gripper assembly parametrically in cad/openscad/. SHARED CONTEXT (same task, three tools, one pebble each so they can run in separate git worktrees): recreate the SO-101 gripper assembly -- the fixed jaw (gripper body) and the moving jaw -- as a baseline for comparing three CAD tools. Jake verbatim: "I want to be able to modify them in the future, so you will have to do it in a way that supports that." That means parametric, editable source. Importing a mesh and calling it done FAILS the test. Use named variables for every dimension that might plausibly change: jaw length, jaw opening, fingertip thickness, servo horn bore, fastener sizes, wall thickness. DIMENSIONAL SOURCE OF TRUTH -- two real SO-101 STEP files are already committed at cad/build123d/reference/: Moving_Jaw_SO101.step and Wrist_Roll_Follower_SO101.step. STEP carries exact analytic geometry, so measure from these. Do NOT re-download them and do NOT invent or eyeball dimensions from tessellated meshes. WHY THIS PART: it is what Jake will modify for the Hand 1.0 paper gripper -- cross-reference plans/hand_1_0.md and plans/gripper_bet.md as reading, and cite them in your notes. DELIVERABLE BESIDES THE MODEL: a NOTES.md in your own tool directory covering time taken, what was easy, what was painful, whether the tool known weakness actually mattered in practice, and how it would feel to modify this part six months from now. State plainly if the geometry ends up approximate and list what still needs verifying. BOUNDARIES: stay inside your own cad/<tool>/ directory and touch nothing else. Do NOT edit plans/hand_1_0.md or plans/gripper_bet.md -- a later pass writes the comparison across all three tools. The other two tool pebbles are running in parallel in their own worktrees, so do not touch cad/openscad/, cad/build123d/, or cad/blender/ other than your own. TOOL SPECIFICS: OpenSCAD is installed at /Applications/OpenSCAD.app; the CLI binary is inside the bundle at /Applications/OpenSCAD.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenSCAD. Write .scad source with a named-variable block at the top. Prove it compiles by rendering a PNG and exporting an STL from the CLI, both committed. Note the reference STEP files live under cad/build123d/reference/ -- read them for dimensions only (OpenSCAD cannot import STEP, so measure and transcribe), and write nothing into that directory. KNOWN LIMITATION TO EVALUATE HONESTLY IN NOTES.md: OpenSCAD is mesh output only -- no B-rep, no true fillets, no STEP export. Does that actually bite on THIS part, or is it irrelevant here? Give a real verdict, not a hedge. The upside to weigh against it: a single self-contained file with no dependencies. MID-FLIGHT CLARIFICATION (added 2026-09-13, AFTER this pebble was claimed and work had started -- read it even if you are already mid-run; it changes what you optimize for, not what you build): WHY WE ARE DOING THIS (the goal is not the gripper -- the goal is choosing the tool). Recreating a part that already exists produces nothing new on its own. Its entire value is as a controlled benchmark. Jake is about to design Hand 1.0 (a paper-handling gripper that mounts to the SO-101 and is also usable handheld) and later Hand 2.0 (a fully 3D-printed human hand identical to its teleop glove). That is a long hardware design programme and it should be done in ONE tool. This exercise decides which one. WHY RECREATE A KNOWN PART SPECIFICALLY: because there is ground truth. The reference STEP files say exactly what the geometry should be, so "did this tool let me express the real part accurately" has a checkable answer -- unlike designing something new, where any result looks plausible and you learn nothing about the tool. WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEING MEASURED (optimize for producing a fair verdict, NOT for finishing fast): (1) Can this tool express real mechanical geometry accurately, from measured dimensions? (2) How painful is it to change a dimension six months later? This matters MORE than initial build speed, because these parts will be iterated many times against measurements that do not exist yet. (3) Does it live well in git -- readable diffs, reviewable history? (4) Can an AGENT author and revise it directly? Jake wants to iterate hardware by voice, which means the format has to be text an agent can reliably write. (5) Is the output actually usable for functional printed parts -- fits, fillets, fasteners, bearing seats? (6) It must be open source. That was Jake's stated requirement. THEREFORE: an honest NOTES.md verdict is the PRIMARY deliverable, equal in value to working geometry. An agent that hits a genuine wall and documents it precisely has done this task correctly. Do NOT paper over friction to make your tool look good -- a tool that loses fairly here saves months of pain later. This decision feeds plans/hand_1_0.md (section 6 records the provisional OpenSCAD-first call that this exercise is meant to confirm or overturn) and plans/gripper_bet.md -- read both, cite them, and still do not edit them. FOR OPENSCAD SPECIFICALLY: plans/hand_1_0.md section 6 already leans OpenSCAD-first, so your job is to stress-test that call rather than vindicate it. If the mesh-only / no-fillet / no-STEP limitation would bite on a fastened, filleted, bearing-seated Hand 1.0 part, say so plainly even though it makes the incumbent look worse. Weigh the single-self-contained-file upside against criteria (2), (3) and (4).
